clue.text: In favour of stuffing exhaust pipe with discarded material

indicators.note: one piece is packed inside the other, as stuffing fills a bird

parts.note: to exhaust resources is to use them up, to waste them
a duct is a pipe or channel
pro is Latin-derived shorthand for in favour of

explanation.surface: A mechanic describes a car's exhaust pipe clogged with rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Byproducts thrown away after manufacture or use are commonly called by this two-word term.

clue.text: Erratic manner leading to conflict with daughter

parts.note: a way of doing something is its manner
war is armed conflict
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A family drama: an erratic lifestyle ends in a feud with one's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unpredictable and hard to control is described with this adjective, a near synonym.

clue.text: Foot prints finally found by lake near the centre of Leek

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word prints

parts.note: a pond is a small lake

indicators.note: the centre of the four-letter word Leek is its two middle letters

explanation.surface: Footprints are discovered beside a lake close to the Staffordshire market town of Leek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' looks like part of 'footprints', but it stands alone as the definition: a metrical foot in poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody, a unit of two stressed syllables is one kind of metrical foot.

clue.text: Make light of Cuba regularly intervening in area close to Suriname

indicators.note: these letters come between the other letters, sitting inside them

parts.note: extent is the area or size something covers

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word Cuba
the close of a word is its last letter, here of Suriname

explanation.surface: A geopolitical note about Cuban influence in a region near Suriname, South America.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen the seriousness of an offence, usually by offering excuses, is to downplay it.

clue.text: Go after half of Ruth's money

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first
half of the name Ruth gives its opening pair of letters

parts.note: to go is a coy way of saying to urinate, to pee

explanation.surface: Someone sets off after part of Ruth's cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a verb of motion; it is the nursery euphemism for urinating.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency unit of India, Pakistan and several other countries.

clue.text: Expressionless god unresponsive at first

indicators.note: at first puts this piece at the front, before the god

parts.note: something dead gives no response, like a dead phone line
Pan is the Greek god of shepherds and the wild

explanation.surface: A statue of a stony-faced deity that fails to react.
explanation.definitionFit: A face showing no emotion, often while joking, is described with this word.

clue.text: Tree house entered with caution for the most part

indicators.note: the house is entered, so the other piece goes inside it

parts.note: casa is Spanish and Italian for house

indicators.note: most of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: care is caution, as in take care

explanation.surface: Someone cautiously enters a house in a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Cascara is a buckthorn of western North America whose bark yields a laxative.

clue.text: Surprisingly elitist rant by conservatoire's principal player

indicators.note: by sets one piece next to the other
the principal, or leading, letter of the word conservatoire's
the words are rearranged in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A shocking snobbish outburst from the head of a music college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal' looks like the college head; it only picks the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind musician playing a reed instrument is a type of player.

clue.text: Displays plans

definitions.meaning: arranges goods or items for show
designs or arranges something in detail, like a garden

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both setting things out for viewing and designing a layout.

clue.text: Priest getting financial assistance to house a couple of Serbians is commended

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside, as a house holds residents

parts.note: aid is help, especially money given to others

indicators.note: a couple of letters from the start of Serbians

explanation.surface: A priest who secures funding to shelter Serbian refugees is praised.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak approvingly of someone is to praise or laud them.

clue.text: Animal's attention held by hollowed out yams for ages

parts.note: a donkey's, the possessive of a beast of burden

indicators.note: this piece is held inside another
a word hollowed out keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: ear means attention, as in have someone's ear

explanation.surface: A beast is distracted by yams with their insides scooped out.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom DONKEY'S YEARS means a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal British idiom means a very long time, punning on donkey's ears being long.

clue.text: Central African girl living in Niger

indicators.note: the girl lives inside the other piece

parts.note: RN is the international vehicle code for Niger
Wanda is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl who makes her home in the West African state of Niger.
explanation.walkthrough: Niger looks like where the girl lives; it only supplies its car code RN.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Rwanda, a small country in central-east Africa, is so called.

clue.text: Account for former partner getting even

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
plain can mean flat or level, as even does

explanation.surface: Someone justifies their ex getting revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting even' suggests revenge; 'even' alone means level or flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To give reasons for something, to clarify or justify it, is what account for means.

clue.text: Gentle reminder from courtroom official with note for Jack

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: a judge presides over a courtroom
J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A court official is handed a memo in place of someone named Jack.
explanation.definitionFit: A light prod or prompt to make someone remember something is a gentle hint.

clue.text: Benefit from old saying about never, at the outset, cutting tax

indicators.note: the saying goes around the rest

parts.note: an adage is a traditional proverb

indicators.note: the letter cuts into the tax, sitting inside it

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax

indicators.note: at the outset takes the opening letter of never

explanation.surface: Someone profits from an old proverb about never cutting taxes at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge or favourable position over others is a benefit.

clue.text: Bitter Victorian stupidly ignoring article embracing the Italian uprising

indicators.note: the jumbled letters wrap around the other piece
done stupidly means put together in a muddled order
ignoring means leaving out the article's letters

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down clue, uprising means read from bottom to top

parts.note: il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: An angry Victorian foolishly backs an Italian revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring article' drops AN from VICTORIAN; 'stupidly' scrambles the rest to VITRIOC; 'uprising' turns IL into LI, which that jumble embraces.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech full of caustic venom, like sulphuric acid's old name, is bitter in tone.

clue.text: Defiantly aggressive criminal culture Unite oddly dismissed

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong, so the letters are rearranged
the odd-numbered letters of Unite are removed, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Union members of Unite throw out a criminal culture.
explanation.walkthrough: Unite is a big British trade union. Dropping its odd letters leaves NT, which joins CULTURE for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A belligerent, fierce and combative person is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Countless piles of rubbish uncovered by youngster

indicators.note: uncovered strips the outer letters away

parts.note: dumps are heaps of rubbish
a teen is a youngster

explanation.surface: A child discovers innumerable heaps of rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal word means a great many, too many to count.

clue.text: Artist introduced to relatives in the heart of Huguenot country

indicators.note: this group sits within the other piece
the heart of Huguenot is its central pair of letters
the artist is introduced into the relatives

parts.note: kin are one's relatives
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter meets family in the Huguenot heartland of France.
explanation.definitionFit: An Eastern European nation bordering Russia and Poland is a country.

clue.text: Goes beyond removing power from fools

indicators.note: removing takes the letter away

parts.note: passes means overtakes or goes beyond
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Someone oversteps, stripping authority from idiots.
explanation.definitionFit: Donkeys are proverbially stupid, so silly people are called by this animal name.

clue.text: Starts to analyse several potential hazards associated with key waterproofing material

indicators.note: starts of each word gives its opening letter

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A safety inspector analyses hazards linked to a waterproofing compound.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitumen-based tarmac used for roofs and roads keeps out water.

clue.text: Conceal son and another relative

parts.note: a mother is another family member

explanation.surface: A family hides a son and a further family member.
explanation.definitionFit: To cover something completely so it is hidden or suppressed is to conceal it.

clue.text: Put at risk after first of attendants abandons sovereign

indicators.note: the letter abandons the word, so is removed

parts.note: imperial means sovereign, of an emperor

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of attendants

explanation.surface: A monarch is deserted by the leading courtier.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger or jeopardise something is to put it at risk.

clue.text: Relating to the law of gravitation originally observed in a field near Luxembourg

indicators.note: the letter is observed inside the field

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of gravitation

parts.note: L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg

explanation.surface: Newton's law of gravitation observed in a meadow near Luxembourg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the law of gravitation' reads as one phrase; the definition stops at 'law'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything concerning or permitted by statute and courts is lawful or juridical.

clue.text: Mischievous child learning to beg

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
lore is traditional knowledge or learning

explanation.surface: A naughty youngster picks up how to plead.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead earnestly or beseech someone is a synonym of beg.

clue.text: Packed with group of players speaking in German

indicators.note: speaking signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: a team is a group of players

explanation.surface: A squad of footballers chatting away in German.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowded or swarming, as a street can be full of people, means packed.

clue.text: Beat poets essentially in a state of agitation

indicators.note: the letter sits inside the other piece

parts.note: to be in a lather is to be agitated

indicators.note: the essence of poets is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Beat poets like Ginsberg in a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat poets' is a known phrase, but 'Beat' is the definition: to thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: To leather someone is informal for thrashing them, as with a strap.

clue.text: One in conversation with neurotic learner driver panicking on hill

indicators.note: panicking means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a learner driver's car
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: A nervous learner driver flustered while stalled on a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A person taking part in a dialogue is a conversational partner.
